standard_prerequisites.name: Baer's criterion in the module case
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the model argument for modules that the proof adapts to an arbitrary Grothendieck abelian category with a generator.

standard_prerequisites.name: Surjections from coproducts of the generator
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the description of objects as quotients of coproducts of copies of a generator
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that a subobject of a source can be reached from subobjects of the generator, which is what reduces the extension problem to the diagrams of the statement.

core_obligations: Setup (proof lines 1688-1692): the author recalls the module case and starts with an injection and a morphism into the candidate injective object.

The reduction (proof lines 1692-1705): the extension problem is reduced to the case where the source is a coproduct of copies of the generator, by writing the subobject as a quotient of such a coproduct, and the hypothesis of the lemma is then applied to subobjects of the generator.

Assembling the extension (proof lines 1705-1712): the extensions obtained on the pieces are compatible by construction and therefore glue to an extension on the whole subobject, which gives the extension property and hence injectivity.
proof_roadmap: Reduce an extension problem to the case where the source is a coproduct of copies of the generator.
Apply the hypothesis to the subobjects of the generator appearing there.
Glue the resulting compatible extensions to get the extension property.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that an object of a Grothendieck abelian category with a generator is injective exactly when every extension problem from a subobject of the generator can be solved (statement lines 1670-1686). The proof is a complete argument: it starts from an arbitrary injection and morphism into the object (proof lines 1688-1692), reduces the extension problem to the case where the source is built from copies of the generator (proof lines 1692-1705), applies the hypothesis on the pieces, and glues the compatible extensions to obtain the extension property, hence injectivity (proof lines 1705-1712). The non-formal content is the reduction to the generator and the gluing. The claim is H2.
